prompt: In 120 to 180 words, compare ranking metrics and classification metrics in exactly four numbered points. Include one search-system example and finish with a one-sentence conclusion.

turns.assistant_message:
Ranking metrics and classification metrics are two essential evaluation methods used in information retrieval systems to assess the performance of search results.

1. Ranking metrics focus on measuring the order or arrangement of documents based on their relevance to a query. Commonly used ranking metrics include Normalized Discounted Cumulative Gain (NDCG), Mean Average Precision (MAP), and Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR). These metrics aim to evaluate how well the most relevant documents are positioned in the search results.

2. Classification metrics, on the other hand, assess the relevance of individual documents without considering their order. Precision, recall, and F1-score are popular
